about.heading: About me
about.p1: Second year of the BI Analyst programme at Nackademin. We work with data warehouses, pull data from databases, APIs and Excel, and build interactive reports in Power BI.
about.p2: Before I started studying I worked as a nurse. That gave me a feel for how an organisation runs day to day — and which decisions the numbers are meant to support.
about.p3: Now I am curious about how a company your size builds its data models behind the scenes.

projects.intro: Projects from the programme at Nackademin. Each one shows the question to be answered, what I built, and where it landed. More are added through the year.
project.part.question: The question
project.star.title: Sales analysis on a star schema
project.star.question: Which articles and stores drive the margin — and why does it differ between quarters?
project.star.did: Loaded raw transaction data into SQL Server, normalised it and rebuilt it as fact and dimension tables. Measures in DAX, a time dimension for year, quarter and month.
project.star.outcome: A report where a store manager gets from year to a single article in three clicks, without needing to know how the model is built.
project.api.title: From API to dashboard
project.api.question: How do you bring in data that changes every day without someone pasting into Excel?
project.api.did: Pulled an open API with Python, handled pagination and missing values, and wrote the result to a database on a schedule.
project.api.outcome: The report refreshes itself. The manual step that usually breaks is simply gone.
project.care.title: Care flow in numbers
project.care.question: Where do the queues build, and is the peak caused by more visits or by fewer staff on duty?
project.care.did: Modelled simulated visit data per unit and month, set target levels, and built measures a ward manager recognises.
project.care.outcome: The project where my healthcare background mattered most — I knew which questions actually get asked at a morning handover.
